clue.text: See 22
Brighton ref nit-picking — hosts raised hell

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the hidden letters are read upwards, so backwards
the phrase Brighton ref nit-picking hosts, or holds inside it, a run of letters

explanation.surface: A fussy football referee in Brighton lets the home side kick up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosts' hides ONREFNI across 'Brighton ref nit', and 'raised' turns it upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a blazing fire and also, from Dante, a name for the underworld of the damned.

clue.text: Copycat is over neat

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals that the word for cat is turned round, reading upwards

parts.note: the Rex is a breed of cat, such as the Cornish Rex
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A copycat looks tidier than the original.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only 'Copy': 'cat' belongs to the wordplay, as the Rex breed of cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerox is a photocopier brand used as a verb meaning to photocopy something.

clue.text: Store outside Santander's affirmative bank

indicators.note: the word for store sits outside, around, the other piece

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse
Santander is a Spanish city, and the Spanish word for yes is si

explanation.surface: A Spanish bank, Santander, approves a branch with a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: Santander is also a Spanish bank, which makes 'bank' look like part of the scene; here Santander just points to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank money is to deposit it, putting it into an account for safekeeping.

clue.text: Cold capital with extremes of temperature that creates a 19 after change

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A chilly capital city with swings of temperature sets off a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is EMERGENCY: add 'change' to the answer and the phrase climate change leads to a climate emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate change is the long-term warming that campaigners say has produced a climate emergency.

clue.text: Network trouble arising that is hampering society

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means the word for trouble reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is hampers, or closes around, the letter for society

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Trouble on the network grows when it gets in society's way.
explanation.definitionFit: To network is to make contacts and keep in touch with others, which is what liaising means.

clue.text: Film the French on strike, a cover for Christmas activities

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist on glass
le is French for the
to toe a ball is to strike it with the tip of the foot

explanation.surface: A French film about a strike, set at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins the pieces: in a down clue, each piece sits on the one below.
explanation.definitionFit: People kiss under a sprig of mistletoe at Christmas, so it hangs over, and gives cover to, festive kissing.

clue.text: Rogue that creates revolutions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a swindler, someone who twists the truth
second meaning: a tornado, a wind that spins round and round

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutions' looks political, as if a rogue starts uprisings; it is the turning of a whirlwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is both a dishonest cheat and an American word for a tornado's spinning funnel of wind.

clue.text: Male inventor sick about Newton becoming green

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the letter for Newton
sick suggests something out of sorts, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: An inventor who is ill over Isaac Newton turns green with envy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' hints at Isaac Newton the scientist, but here it gives the unit symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: Green, in politics, describes concern for the natural world, the same idea as environmental.

clue.text: A service that's revolutionary at a distance

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word for the service is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A branch of the armed forces with radical ideas operates far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar is an old-fashioned adverb for far away, as in seen from afar.

clue.text: Confine guy's joint and hand

parts.note: to pen is to shut in, as with sheep
a guy is a man, so a guy's is a man's
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A man's hand and hip are put in a splint.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand here means handwriting, as in a neat hand, and penmanship is the skill or style of writing.

clue.text: Endless dirt: it is recurrent, creating baffling problems

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for dirt is dropped

parts.note: crud is slang for dirt or filth

indicators.note: recurrent is read as running back, so the word for it is reversed

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, or sex itself

explanation.surface: Mud that keeps coming back sets puzzling problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is crossword slang for sex, as in the 'It girl'; 'is' joins it to 'recurrent', which reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruxes are the central, hardest points of a problem, the knots that are baffling to untie.

clue.text: Cushion Brown left in Oman, possibly

indicators.note: left is read as departed, so the word for brown goes out of the rest

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate, a state ruled by a sultan; possibly marks it as one example
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: Someone called Brown, gone off to Oman, is cushioned from trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a person's name; it is the colour TAN, which leaves IN + SULTANATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cushion something is to protect it from shocks, as insulation shields from heat, noise or harm.

clue.text: 9 this from recycled plutonium — guards look back, leaving depleted uranium

indicators.note: recycled means the letters of plutonium are reprocessed into a new order
leaving means the letters from depleted uranium are taken away from that pool
plutonium guards, or keeps with it, the reversed word for look, adding it to the pool
back means the word for look is read in reverse

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold

indicators.note: depleted is taken as emptied of its middle, leaving only the first and last letters of uranium

explanation.surface: Reprocessed plutonium is guarded, and depleted uranium is the waste left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is ENVIRONMENTAL, so the definition is the second word of environmental pollution. 'depleted' empties uranium of its middle, and the letters that remain leave the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmental pollution is the harmful contamination of air, water and land with waste.

clue.text: Attack in California city bay, a start to tragedy

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, a city in California
to bay is to bark or howl, so to shout loudly

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tragedy begins in a Californian bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests a stretch of coastline; here it is the verb, as a hound bays.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out at someone is to attack them suddenly with blows or words.

clue.text: Expressionist artist's content to get things moving

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what it holds inside, so the letters are found within it

explanation.surface: An Expressionist painter is happy enough to get things going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like the adjective for happy, but it is the noun: what the words hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To start something is to set it going, to begin the action.

clue.text: Charlotte's discrimination shown in a brief device

definitions.note: Charlotte is a US city, pointing to the American spelling without the E

indicators.note: brief means the last letter of the word for device is cut off

parts.note: a gismo, or gizmo, is a gadget or device

explanation.surface: A woman called Charlotte is victimised by a short gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlotte' looks like a woman's name; it is the city in North Carolina, pointing to the spelling preferred in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Agism is prejudice against people because of their age, the same as ageism.

clue.text: Stick lettuce inside something sweet

indicators.note: the word for lettuce goes inside the word for stick

parts.note: glue is something that makes things stick
cos is a type of lettuce, called romaine in the US

explanation.surface: A lettuce leaf is pressed into a sugary treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, the sweet substance in fruit and honey.

clue.text: Crisis with English vehicle missing a crossing over French sea

indicators.note: the outer letters straddle, or cross over, the French word for sea
missing means the letter A is lost from the word for vehicle

parts.note: an agency is a means or vehicle by which something is done
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: An English car breaks down while crossing the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' looks like a car, but it means a channel or means: AGENCY, from which 'missing' drops A. E + GENCY then crosses over MER.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation needing immediate action, which is a crisis.

clue.text: Again class note German artist of French extraction

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
de is French for of or from, as in names showing a family's origin

explanation.surface: A French-born German painter is put in another category.
explanation.definitionFit: To regrade is to assess or sort something into a class a second time.

clue.text: Annoyance of old king hampered by restraint

indicators.note: the old king is hampered by being held inside the restraint

parts.note: a chain is a restraint, as on a prisoner
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: An old king is annoyed at being held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation, especially the irritation of being disappointed or humiliated.

clue.text: Battered cod boxed in air or gas

indicators.note: battered means beaten about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Battered cod, boxed up in the open air or fried in oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' looks like fish shop language; it is the anagram signal. 'or' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide is the colourless greenhouse gas breathed out by animals and released by burning fuel.

clue.text: Fast route from A to B, then regularly dashing around university

indicators.note: the other letters go around the letter for university
regularly means every other letter of dashing is taken

explanation.surface: Getting from A to B, then rushing round a university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A to B' is taken literally as letters, and 'regularly' gives AHN, the second, fourth and sixth letters of dashing.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a road built for fast travel.

clue.text: International, where young woman crosses pitch

indicators.note: the girl crosses, or spans, the pitch, holding it inside

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman
to lob is to pitch or throw a ball high

explanation.surface: A young woman runs across a sports field, playing at international level.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means worldwide, involving the whole world rather than one nation.

clue.text: Energy zero — not moving!

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O
not moving is travelling at zero miles per hour, written 0 mph

explanation.surface: Zero energy: completely still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not moving' is read as a speed, 0 mph, with the zero as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour, enthusiasm and get-up-and-go.

clue.text: Where tourists go to order cava and roast beef starter

indicators.note: putting letters to order arranges them anew
a starter is what comes first, so the first letter of beef

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers go to order sparkling wine and roast beef as a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa Brava is the Spanish coast in Catalonia, a popular resort area for holidaymakers.

clue.text: Book character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a book of the Bible, the second Gospel
second meaning: a written sign or symbol

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a character in a novel; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of Mark is a New Testament book, and a mark is a written symbol or sign.

clue.text: Dispersing a thing full of energy

definitions.text: Dispersing a thing full of energy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are full of, hold inside, the letter for energy
dispersing means scattering, so the letters of a thing are spread into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Something packed with energy is being spread about.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: heating spreads energy into a thing. With 24 it makes global heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Heating transfers thermal energy into something, warming the object up.

clue.text: Men hate cooking — it contributes to 24 28

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of men hate are prepared in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Men refuse to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 28 is GLOBAL HEATING, the warming of the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas, released by livestock and landfill, that adds to global warming.
